summary: New London County, CT: in 1951 the state forestry department was building a tower on Stewart Hill near Wyassup Lake to replace the Fort Hill tower; a 1968 bid lists it as 75 feet tall; Forest Lookouts marks it removed; no source describes the site today.

facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts marks the tower Removed; no date or method given
facts.agency: Connecticut state forestry department (1951 report); State Park and Forest Commission (1968 bid)

events.note: February 1951 report (quoted by Forest Lookouts from The Day): the tower was being constructed by the state forestry department on Stewart Hill near Wyassup lake, to replace the Fort Hill tower
February 1968 bid notice (quoted from The Bridgeport Post): painting and repairs for six state forest fire towers, April 1 to June 30, 1968, including the 75-foot Stewart Hill tower

evidence.supports: in February 1951 the state forestry department was constructing a new tower on Stewart Hill near Wyassup Lake to serve most of New London County
evidence.quote: A new forest fire observation tower to serve most of New London county is being constructed by the state forestry department on Stewart Hill near Wyassup lake

evidence.supports: the 1951 report was from The Day
the new tower would replace the tower on Fort Hill just outside Mystic
evidence.quote: The new tower, when completed will replace the one now located on Fort Hill just outside Mystic.

evidence.supports: the Fort Hill tower would stay in use until the new one was ready
evidence.quote: the tower atop Fort Hill will be used until the new one is ready

evidence.supports: in February 1968 the State Park and Forest Commission invited sealed bids
evidence.quote: Sealed bids addressed to the Director of the State Park and Forest Commission of the State of Connecticut for:

evidence.supports: the 1968 bid covered painting and repairing six forest fire towers between April 1 and June 30, 1968
evidence.quote: The painting and repairing of six forest fire towers during the period April 1, 1968 through June 30, 1968.

evidence.supports: the Stewart Hill tower was 75 feet high and on the 1968 list
evidence.quote: the 75-foot high tower at Stewart Hill

evidence.supports: Forest Lookouts marks the tower removed
Wyassup Lake is in North Stonington, New London County, Connecticut
evidence.quote: Wyassup Lake in North Stonington is in New London County, Connecticut

notes_for_editor: The 1951 and 1968 items are newspaper text quoted on Forest Lookouts; the originals were not read. Fort Hill record (firetower.org/lookouts/us/ct/fort-hill-tower-site/, US 66, CT 5) says its steel tower was eventually moved to North Stonington. The sources read do not say whether that tower is the Stewart Hill tower, so the story does not link them; an editor may want to check. The 1951 spotter sentence refers to the Fort Hill tower, not Stewart Hill, so staffing is left out. Agency names differ between 1951 (state forestry department) and 1968 (State Park and Forest Commission); both are recorded and not reconciled. ExploreCT Stewart Hill Preserve page (explorect.org) is JavaScript-rendered and returned 403 to WebFetch; a search snippet describing a town park was not read, so no access or site-today claim is made from it.
